turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi, how are you holding up?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm doing a murder mystery party for my birthday. How do I word the invitation?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fun. Make the invitation feel like part of the story. Do you have a setting yet?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A nineteen twenties country house. Very dramatic.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then something like, you are cordially summoned to Blackwood Manor, where one guest will not survive the evening. Dress for the era.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ooh. Should I give people their characters in advance?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, a week ahead, with a short secret only they know. It gets people excited and they'll put more effort into costumes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: are going to be terrible actors.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's half the fun. Give the shy ones smaller roles, like the butler, so they can join in without pressure.
